metadata.title: The Mycelial Humanities: Collective Wisdom & Commoning
metadata.notes: Foundational humanities for a decentralized, high-trust society.

nodes.title: Biological Reciprocity (IKS)
nodes.description: Learning from the living substrate. Indigenous perspectives on land stewardship, medicinal plants, and the ethics of taking only what is needed. Grounding Ubuntu in ecology.

nodes.title: History of the Commons
nodes.description: Before the State and the Market: how humans managed shared water, forests, and knowledge for millennia. Elinor Ostrom's 8 principles for managing the commons.

nodes.title: Collaborative Sense-Making
nodes.description: Techniques for collective intelligence: Socratic dialogue, Non-Violent Communication (NVC), and identifying logical fallacies in real-time group settings.

nodes.title: Restorative Justice Circles
nodes.description: Moving from punitive to restorative justice. The architecture of the 'Healing Circle' and the role of the community in repairing trust after a violation.

nodes.title: The Ubuntu Stewardship Capstone
nodes.description: Facilitate a real-world community dialogue or manage a shared resource project (e.g., a community tool library) using the principles of the commons and restorative justice.

holonic_capstone.deliverable: A verified record of community facilitation or resource management, endorsed by the affected Learning Pod.

edges.rationale: Stewardship requires understanding the historical principles of the commons.
Effective stewardship requires advanced collaborative sense-making.
Resolving community conflict is a core skill for long-term stewardship.
Ecological reciprocity provides the spiritual grounding for physical stewardship.
